mechanics.name: Soul Guard
mechanics.currentEffect: Whenever you heal or recover from the Dying State, gain Endurance for 4/6/8 seconds. Endurance is cancelled early if you perform a Conspicuous Action. This effect has a 30-second cooldown. While Cursed, you can fully recover from the Dying State using Self-Recovery.
activation: Heal or recover from the Dying State to trigger Endurance.
Be Cursed by a Hex effect to unlock Self-Recovery from the Dying State.
Ends/deactivates when: Endurance ends after 4/6/8 seconds or early after a Conspicuous Action.
Ends/deactivates when: Self-Recovery from Dying is available only while Cursed.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (4.7.0): Added a 30-second cooldown between Endurance activations.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: Healing or recovering grants brief Endurance, and being affected by a Hex lets you fully recover from the Dying State.
specialInteractions: The self-recovery effect is conditional on being affected by a Hex; the Endurance trigger has a separate 30-second cooldown.

editorial.summary: After being healed or recovering from the Dying State, gain brief Endurance; while Cursed, you can also fully self-recover from the ground.
useCases: Prevent an immediate re-down after a teammate or perk gets you off the ground.
Pair with Conviction or Unbreakable so a self-pick has a protected escape window.
Exploit the unlimited self-recovery clause in matches where you are Cursed.
counters: Endurance only lasts up to 8 seconds and is cancelled by a Conspicuous Action.
The normal Endurance trigger requires first getting out of the Dying State.
The Cursed self-recovery clause depends on a Hex-related condition the Survivor does not fully control.
pros: Protects the vulnerable moment immediately after a ground recovery.
Excellent synergy with several strong anti-slug perks.
Can become dramatically stronger in Cursed matches.
cons: Provides no value before a Dying-State recovery occurs.
Part of its ceiling depends on the Killer bringing a relevant Hex effect.
analysis: Soul Guard ranks this position because getting off the ground is not always enough. A Killer can immediately hit a freshly recovered Survivor and erase the entire rescue. Soul Guard adds up to eight seconds of Endurance after the recovery, forcing the Killer to respect that brief protection window.

The perk has become especially relevant alongside Conviction. Conviction creates a temporary self-pick, while Soul Guard can protect the first hit after standing. Unbreakable and Boon: Exponential create similar combinations. In those builds, Soul Guard acts as the safety layer that turns recovery into actual movement rather than an instant re-down.

The Cursed clause can be extraordinary but should not dominate the ranking. When active, full self-recovery becomes available without the usual one-use restriction, but Survivors cannot rely on every Killer bringing a Hex that places them in the relevant state. We treat that as upside rather than baseline value.

Soul Guard remains B because its activation is reactive and specific. Matches without meaningful slugging can leave it nearly invisible. In slug-heavy matches, however, it is one of the best support pieces for a recovery-focused build.
editorial.verdict: A strong anti-slug companion perk. Soul Guard is most valuable when another effect already gets you off the ground and you need protection long enough to actually escape.
